name: last_30_min_momentum_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, the 14:45-15:20 closing window sees concentrated institutional order flow as VWAP-benchmarked funds must fill their final allocations before the 15:30 close. When NIFTY has accumulated a >0.3% directional day return and remains on the correct side of session VWAP at 14:45, these late institutional orders reinforce the day's direction in 30-90 second micro-bursts — not one sustained push but sequential order batches from different fund managers executing their end-of-day mandates at staggered times. At 5-second resolution we detect each burst as it begins (positive 1-minute momentum aligning with the day direction) rather than taking a single time-based entry held through noise until 15:29.

indicators.name: day_return
indicators.purpose: Cumulative measure from 09:15 session open — no scaling needed; fixed time window regardless of bar size. Original used 1% on individual stocks; NIFTY index is ~5x less volatile than individual Nifty50 names, so 0.3% on NIFTY represents the same 'meaningful directional day' signal. Below 0.3%, end-of-day flows are mixed and no consistent closing imbalance exists.

indicators.name: session_vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume) from first bar of day
indicators.purpose: Cumulative session VWAP — no scaling needed. Directly adapted from original: close > VWAP confirms intraday buy-side flow has dominated and VWAP-benchmarked algorithms still have closing buy interest (they are below their benchmark cost and must buy to close tracking error). Close < VWAP signals the reverse.

indicators.name: mom_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute momentum (12 x 5s bars) as trade trigger. The original used a single fixed entry at 14:45 with no intra-window trigger; at 5s resolution we need to detect each institutional burst as it fires. 12 bars (1 min) is correct for this trigger: we hold 30-90s, so a burst must be visible at 1-min scale to carry forward. Shorter (6 bars / 30s) is too noisy at 5s; longer (60 bars / 5 min) misses the burst entry point and is a context filter not a trigger.

conditions: close > session_vwap (price above average buy price — institutional longs in profit, extending into close)
mom_12 > 0.0005 (positive 1-min momentum confirming a burst is firing)
buy_ce.confirmation: All four conditions true simultaneously on a 5s bar

conditions: close < session_vwap (price below average cost — institutional shorts adding or longs cutting)
mom_12 < -0.0005 (negative 1-min momentum confirming a selling burst)
buy_pe.confirmation: All four conditions true simultaneously on a 5s bar

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts = ~8 NIFTY spot pts at ATM delta 0.5. Last-30-min institutional momentum that reverses >8 spot points within 30s means the closing buy/sell imbalance was exhausted or mis-read; the thesis is invalidated. NIFTY typical 30s moves are 2-5 option pts, so 4 pts is a 1.5-2σ adverse move — a clear signal the burst failed rather than normal choppiness.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option pts = ~12 NIFTY spot pts at ATM delta 0.5. Typical last-30-min institutional burst on NIFTY covers 15-25 spot points in a 30-90s window; targeting 12 pts captures 50-80% of the median burst, achieving 1:1.5 R:R (4 stop : 6 target). Conservative sizing because 4-6 such trades per session compound the edge without requiring a full 25-pt run on every entry.

filters.vix_filter: none — closing institutional mandates execute regardless of VIX regime; fund managers must meet NAV reporting regardless of volatility
filters.time_filter: active only 14:45-15:20 IST; no signals outside this 35-minute window
filters.volume_filter: none — index volume is implicitly captured in session VWAP computation
filters.trend_filter: day_return > 0.3% ensures we only trade on days with meaningful directional conviction
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close prices

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — institutional closing flow is structural, driven by SEBI regulations on mutual fund NAV reporting and end-of-day mandate constraints that are unlikely to change

adaptation_notes: Original screened individual NIFTY50 stocks for day_return > 1% + volume + VWAP alignment, entering at a fixed 14:45 and holding to 15:29 as a single time-based position. Three key changes for 5s NIFTY index options: (1) Universe collapsed from 50 stocks to the NIFTY index itself — the same institutional closing flow that drives individual stock momentum aggregates to measurable index-level momentum; (2) Day return threshold reduced from 1% to 0.3% — NIFTY is ~5x less volatile than individual Nifty50 names, so 0.3% index return represents equivalent directional conviction; (3) Single fixed-time entry replaced by dynamic within-window entries triggered by 1-min momentum — at 5s resolution we capture each institutional burst as it fires rather than sitting through the entire 44-minute window as one position. Volume filter dropped (original's volume_vs_avg > 0.8) because on the index, the day_return > 0.3% + VWAP filter already implies above-average activity; ATR-based stop replaced by fixed option premium points calibrated to typical NIFTY 30-90s move sizes.
weaknesses: Active for only 35 minutes per day (14:45-15:20) — no signals outside this window means zero trades on non-directional or choppy days
On V-shaped reversal days (large gap down then full recovery), day_return may be near zero at 14:45 despite intraday momentum — strategy skips these
Consecutive bursts in same direction can produce multiple entries within minutes; max_trades_per_day=6 limits but does not eliminate cluster risk
Monthly index expiry days see rebalancing flows that can reverse mid-burst against the day trend
